sources.title: Common Lisp MAP over multiple sequences
sources.sections_read: MAP syntax, description, examples, exceptions, footer.
sources.confirmed: MAP invokes a function on matching indexed elements from all supplied sequences and produces a result whose length is the shortest input length. The inspected page has a 1996–2005 copyright range but no verified publication date for the revision.
sources.limits: Common Lisp's sequence type system differs from custom Python indexing objects, and explicit result-type and function arguments leave the discoverability question unresolved. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C07.json.

sources.title: SRFI 1 variadic zip and reference implementation
sources.version_or_date: Live master source listing; exact revision date not verified.
sources.sections_read: Public source listing; zip definition; surrounding list helpers and map-in-order implementation.
sources.confirmed: The source exposes zip as a wrapper composing map and a list constructor, and provides further list-processing implementation material. This was code-through-web inspection after a blocked native endpoint attempt.
sources.limits: Scheme list primitives and mapping semantics require a Python sequence-protocol adapter; inspected code revision is undated and the current specification contains later errata. sources.title: Standard ML ListPair positional pairing in the 1995 basis draft
sources.version_or_date: A New Initial Basis for Standard ML, draft dated 1995-06-26.
sources.sections_read: Cover; ListPair manual page, printed page 53 / zero-based PDF page 60.
sources.confirmed: The draft describes ListPair.zip as pairing corresponding elements and ignoring the longer list's remaining tail, with map and app defined using the paired traversal. The cover is dated 1995-06-26 and that manual page says last change 1994-11-15.
sources.limits: The dated interface handles two lists, so arbitrary arity and indexing objects require adaptation; strict zipEq is visible only in separately inspected later generated documentation and is not backdated. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C07.json.

sources.title: SGI STL binary transform over input iterators
sources.version_or_date: Undated mirror of SGI STL documentation; footer copyright 1993–2001.
sources.sections_read: Binary transform prototype, description, input-iterator requirements, preconditions, example, footer.
sources.confirmed: Binary transform applies an operation to corresponding elements from two input ranges. Its first range controls iteration and the second must contain enough elements; the mirror's footer includes 2001 but gives no verified publication date.
sources.limits: Only the first range has an end parameter; the second must be long enough, so safe shortest-input behavior requires additional checks and a separate row-producing wrapper. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C07.json.
